form.zh: 母音ㅏ・ㅗ → -아서　其他 → -어서　하다 → 해서
form.en: ㅏ/ㅗ → -아서　others → -어서　하다 → 해서

explain.zh: 前一個動作完成後，在那個狀態下接著做下一個，兩個動作緊密相關：친구를 만나서 영화를 봤어요（和朋友見面後一起看了電影）、학교에 가서 공부해요（去學校念書）。
explain.en: The first action leads into the second, closely connected: 친구를 만나서 영화를 봤어요 (I met a friend and we saw a film), 학교에 가서 공부해요 (I go to school and study there).

notes.zh: 和「-고」比：「-고」只是先後順序；「-아서」是前一個動作的結果延續到下一個（同一個地點、同一個對象）。
notes.en: -고 is mere order; -아서 carries the first action into the second (same place or person).

notes.zh: 「-아서」前面不加過去式。
notes.en: No past tense before -아서.

mistakes.zh: 去了學校、在學校念書，用「-아서」比較自然。
mistakes.en: Going and then studying there is naturally -아서.

examples.zh: 和朋友見面後一起看了電影。
examples.en: I met a friend and we saw a film.
I go to school and study there.
I washed the apple and ate it.

quiz.zh: 和朋友見面後一起看了電影。
quiz.en: I met a friend and we saw a film.
I go to school and study there.
I washed the apple and ate it.
I went to the library and borrowed a book.
I wrote a letter to my friend and sent it.

quiz.zh: 昨天見了朋友，一起吃了晚餐。
quiz.en: Yesterday I met a friend and we had dinner together.

form.zh: 母音ㅏ・ㅗ → -아서　其他 → -어서　하다 → 해서　名詞 → 이라서/라서
form.en: ㅏ/ㅗ → -아서　others → -어서　하다 → 해서　nouns → 이라서/라서

explain.zh: 表示原因：배가 고파서 밥을 먹었어요（肚子餓所以吃飯了）、비가 와서 집에 있었어요（下雨所以待在家）。
explain.en: Gives a reason: 배가 고파서 밥을 먹었어요 (I was hungry, so I ate), 비가 와서 집에 있었어요 (it rained, so I stayed in).

notes.zh: 「-아서」後面不能接命令或邀請（×비가 와서 우산을 가져가세요），要改用「-(으)니까」（TOPIK 2）。
notes.en: -아서 can't be followed by a command or suggestion — use -(으)니까 for those.

notes.zh: 道歉、感謝常用：늦어서 죄송해요（遲到了很抱歉）、와 주셔서 감사합니다。
notes.en: Common in apologies and thanks: 늦어서 죄송해요, 와 주셔서 감사합니다.

mistakes.zh: 「-아서」前面不加過去式，時態放在最後。
mistakes.en: No past before -아서; the tense goes at the end.
A request after it needs -(으)니까, not -아서.

examples.en: I was hungry, so I ate.
It rained, so I stayed at home.
Sorry I'm late.

quiz.en: I was hungry, so I ate.
It rained, so I stayed in.
Sorry I'm late.

quiz.zh: 昨天太累了，所以很早就睡了。
quiz.en: I was so tired yesterday that I went to bed early.
Thank you for helping me.
The roads were jammed, so I was late.

form.zh: 語幹沒有收尾音或收尾音是ㄹ ＋ 면　有收尾音 ＋ 으면　名詞 ＋ (이)면
form.en: stem without 받침 or ending in ㄹ + 면　with 받침 + 으면　noun + (이)면

explain.zh: 表示條件「如果～」：비가 오면 집에 있을 거예요（如果下雨就待在家）、시간이 있으면 같이 가요（有時間的話一起去吧）。
explain.en: A condition, “if”: 비가 오면 집에 있을 거예요 (if it rains, I'll stay in), 시간이 있으면 같이 가요 (if you have time, let's go together).

notes.zh: 收尾音是ㄹ時直接加「면」：살다 → 살면。
notes.en: A ㄹ stem just adds 면: 살다 → 살면.

mistakes.zh: 說未來的條件用現在形「오면」。

examples.en: If it rains, I'll stay at home.
If you have time, let's go together.
Ask if you don't know.

quiz.en: If it rains, I'll stay in.
If you have time, let's go.
Ask if you don't know.

quiz.zh: 吃了這個藥的話，很快就會好。
quiz.en: If you take this medicine, you'll get better soon.

quiz.zh: 來韓國的話一定要聯絡我。
quiz.en: If you come to Korea, be sure to get in touch.

quiz.zh: 有時間的話一起看電影吧。
quiz.en: If you have time, let's watch a film together.

form.zh: 形容詞語幹沒有收尾音 ＋ ㄴ（예쁜 꽃）　有收尾音 ＋ 은（작은 가방）　있다/없다 ＋ 는（맛있는 음식）
form.en: adj stem without 받침 + ㄴ (예쁜 꽃)　with 받침 + 은 (작은 가방)　있다/없다 + 는 (맛있는 음식)

explain.zh: 形容詞放在名詞前面修飾它：예쁜 꽃（漂亮的花）、작은 가방（小包包）。「맛있다、재미있다」這類有「있다/없다」的用「는」：맛있는 음식（好吃的食物）。
explain.en: To describe a noun, put the adjective in front: 예쁜 꽃 (a pretty flower), 작은 가방 (a small bag). Adjectives ending in 있다/없다 take 는: 맛있는 음식 (delicious food).

notes.zh: 收尾音是ㅂ的形容詞會變：춥다 → 추운、덥다 → 더운。
notes.en: ㅂ adjectives change: 춥다 → 추운, 덥다 → 더운.

notes.zh: 收尾音是ㄹ的會脫落：길다 → 긴、멀다 → 먼。
notes.en: ㄹ drops: 길다 → 긴, 멀다 → 먼.

examples.en: I bought a pretty flower.
I want to eat something delicious.
It's cold weather today.

quiz.en: I bought a pretty flower.
I want something delicious.
It's cold weather today.
I can't really eat spicy food.

quiz.zh: 頭髮長的那個女生是我姊姊。
quiz.en: The girl with long hair is my older sister.
I like quiet cafés.

title.zh: 動詞接名詞（正在～的、會～的）

form.zh: 動詞語幹 ＋ 는 ＋ 名詞（收尾音ㄹ會脫落：살다 → 사는）
form.en: verb stem + 는 + noun (ㄹ drops: 살다 → 사는)

explain.zh: 用動詞修飾名詞，表示現在或習慣：지금 보는 영화（現在在看的電影）、제가 자주 가는 카페（我常去的咖啡廳）。
explain.en: A verb describing a noun, present or habitual: 지금 보는 영화 (the film I'm watching), 제가 자주 가는 카페 (the café I often go to).

notes.zh: 和中文語序一樣，修飾語放在名詞前面：我常去的咖啡廳 → 자주 가는 카페。
notes.en: Same order as Chinese: the description comes before the noun.

mistakes.zh: 收尾音是ㄹ的動詞，ㄹ脫落再加「는」。
mistakes.en: ㄹ verbs drop ㄹ before 는.
To describe a noun, use the -는 form.

examples.zh: 現在在看的電影很有趣。
examples.en: The film I'm watching now is fun.
This is the café I often go to.
I have a friend who lives in Seoul.

quiz.en: This is the café I often go to.
I have a friend who lives in Seoul.

quiz.zh: 現在在看的電影很有趣。
quiz.en: The film I'm watching is fun.
Who's that person singing over there?

quiz.zh: 住在這附近的人大部分是學生。
quiz.en: Most people who live around here are students.

quiz.zh: 現在正在喝咖啡的人是我朋友。
quiz.en: The person drinking coffee now is my friend.

form.zh: 動詞語幹沒有收尾音 ＋ ㄴ（본 영화）　有收尾音 ＋ 은（먹은 음식）
form.en: verb stem without 받침 + ㄴ (본 영화)　with 받침 + 은 (먹은 음식)

explain.zh: 表示已經發生的動作修飾名詞：어제 본 영화（昨天看的電影）、점심에 먹은 음식（午餐吃的東西）。
explain.en: A past action describing a noun: 어제 본 영화 (the film I saw yesterday), 점심에 먹은 음식 (what I ate for lunch).

notes.zh: 未來用「-(으)ㄹ」：내일 볼 영화（明天要看的電影）。
notes.en: Future is -(으)ㄹ: 내일 볼 영화.

mistakes.zh: 昨天已經看過，要用過去的「본」。

examples.en: The film I saw yesterday was fun.
What I had for lunch was good.
These are clothes I bought in Korea.

quiz.en: The film I saw yesterday was fun.
What I had for lunch was good.
Clothes I bought in Korea.

quiz.zh: 昨天在市場買的水果真的很甜。
quiz.en: The fruit I bought at the market yesterday is really sweet.

quiz.zh: 上週聽的那首歌叫什麼名字？
quiz.en: What's the title of the song you heard last week?
This is the cake I made yesterday.

form.zh: 語幹沒有收尾音 ＋ ㄹ 때　有收尾音 ＋ 을 때　名詞 ＋ 때
form.en: stem without 받침 + ㄹ 때　with 받침 + 을 때　noun + 때

explain.zh: 表示「～的時候」：심심할 때 음악을 들어요（無聊的時候聽音樂）、어릴 때 부산에 살았어요（小時候住在釜山）。名詞直接加「때」：방학 때（放假的時候）。
explain.en: “When …”: 심심할 때 음악을 들어요 (when I'm bored I listen to music), 어릴 때 부산에 살았어요 (I lived in Busan as a child). Nouns just add 때: 방학 때 (during the holidays).

notes.zh: 已經完成的動作用「-았/었을 때」：한국에 갔을 때（去韓國的時候）。
notes.en: For a completed action: -았/었을 때 (한국에 갔을 때).

examples.en: When I'm bored, I listen to music.
I lived in Busan as a child.
I'll travel during the holidays.

quiz.en: When I'm bored, I listen to music.
I'll travel during the holidays.
I watch TV while eating.

quiz.zh: 下雨的時候一定要帶傘。
quiz.en: Be sure to take an umbrella when it rains.

quiz.zh: 第一次來韓國的時候，一句韓語都不會。
quiz.en: When I first came to Korea, I didn't know any Korean.

quiz.zh: 有時間的時候請打電話。
quiz.en: Call me when you have time.

form.zh: 母音ㅏ・ㅗ → -아야 해요　其他 → -어야 해요　하다 → 해야 해요
form.en: ㅏ/ㅗ → -아야 해요　others → -어야 해요　하다 → 해야 해요

explain.zh: 表示義務、必須：내일까지 숙제를 해야 해요（明天前得寫完作業）、일찍 일어나야 해요（得早起）。「해요」也可以換成「돼요」：가야 돼요。
explain.en: Obligation: 내일까지 숙제를 해야 해요 (I have to finish my homework by tomorrow), 일찍 일어나야 해요 (I have to get up early). 해요 can be 돼요: 가야 돼요.

notes.zh: 「不必～」是「-지 않아도 돼요」或「안 -아도 돼요」。
notes.en: “Don't have to” is -지 않아도 돼요 or 안 -아도 돼요.

examples.en: I have to do my homework by tomorrow.
I have to get up early.
I have to take medicine.

quiz.en: I have to do homework.
I have to get up early.
I have to take medicine.

quiz.q: 내일 시험이 있어서 오늘 밤에 공부를（　）해요.
quiz.zh: 明天有考試，所以今晚得念書。
quiz.en: I have an exam tomorrow, so I have to study tonight.

quiz.zh: 這個文法很難，得聽好幾次。
quiz.en: This grammar is hard, so you have to listen several times.
I have to get up early tomorrow.

title.zh: 因為～（後面可接請求、建議）

form.zh: 語幹沒有收尾音或收尾音是ㄹ（ㄹ脫落）＋ 니까　有收尾音 ＋ 으니까
form.en: stem without 받침 or ㄹ (dropped) + 니까　with 받침 + 으니까

explain.zh: 表示原因，後面可以接命令、請求、建議（「-아서」不行）：비가 오니까 우산을 가져가세요（下雨了，帶把傘去吧）、추우니까 문을 닫읍시다（很冷，把門關上吧）。
explain.en: Gives a reason and, unlike -아서, can be followed by commands, requests and suggestions: 비가 오니까 우산을 가져가세요 (it's raining, so take an umbrella), 추우니까 문을 닫읍시다 (it's cold — let's shut the door).

notes.zh: 前面可以加過去式：어제 늦게 잤으니까 피곤해요。
notes.en: Can take the past: 어제 늦게 잤으니까 피곤해요.

examples.en: It's raining, so take an umbrella.
It's cold — let's shut the door.

examples.zh: 沒時間了，搭計程車好嗎？
examples.en: We're short of time — shall we take a taxi?

quiz.en: It's raining, so take an umbrella.

quiz.zh: 沒時間了，搭計程車好嗎？
quiz.en: We're short of time — taxi?
It's cold — let's shut the door.

quiz.zh: 天氣很熱，請把窗戶打開一下。
quiz.en: It's hot, so please open the window.

quiz.zh: 這家餐廳總是人很多，我們早點去吧。
quiz.en: This restaurant is always crowded, so let's go early.
We don't have time, so let's go quickly.

form.zh: 動詞語幹 ＋ 기 전에　／　名詞 ＋ 전에
form.en: verb stem + 기 전에　/　noun + 전에

explain.zh: 表示「在做～之前」：자기 전에 이를 닦아요（睡前刷牙）、식사 전에 손을 씻으세요（用餐前請洗手）。
explain.en: “Before doing …”: 자기 전에 이를 닦아요 (I brush my teeth before bed), 식사 전에 손을 씻으세요 (wash your hands before eating).

notes.zh: 時間長度加「전에」是「～前」：3년 전에（三年前）。
notes.en: A length of time + 전에 means “… ago”: 3년 전에.

examples.en: I brush my teeth before going to bed.
Please wash your hands before eating.

examples.zh: 來韓國之前學了韓文字母。
examples.en: I learned Hangul before coming to Korea.

quiz.en: I brush my teeth before bed.
Wash your hands before eating.

quiz.zh: 來韓國之前學了韓文字母。
quiz.en: I learned Hangul before coming to Korea.
Please call before you come.
I booked a hotel before going on the trip.
I read before going to sleep.

form.zh: 動詞語幹沒有收尾音 ＋ ㄴ 후에　有收尾音 ＋ 은 후에　／　名詞 ＋ 후에
form.en: verb stem without 받침 + ㄴ 후에　with 받침 + 은 후에　/　noun + 후에

explain.zh: 表示「做完～之後」：밥을 먹은 후에 산책해요（吃完飯後散步）、수업 후에 만나요（下課後見）。「후에」也可以說「다음에」。
explain.en: “After doing …”: 밥을 먹은 후에 산책해요 (I take a walk after eating), 수업 후에 만나요 (let's meet after class). 후에 can also be 다음에.

notes.zh: 和「-기 전에」相反；兩個都不在前面加過去式。
notes.en: The opposite of -기 전에; neither takes a past tense before it.

examples.en: I take a walk after eating.
Let's meet after class.
After graduating I want to work in Korea.

quiz.en: I take a walk after eating.
Let's meet after class.
After graduating I want to work in Korea.
I'll go to the library after class.

quiz.zh: 在首爾住了三年後回故鄉了。
quiz.en: After living in Seoul for three years, I went back home.
Let's meet after work is over.

title.zh: ～完之後（做完一件事再做下一件）

form.zh: 動詞詞幹 ＋ -고 나서（有沒有收音都一樣）
form.en: verb stem + -고 나서 (same after any stem)

explain.zh: 前一個動作完全做完以後，才做下一個，重點在「做完」：숙제를 하고 나서 게임을 해요（寫完作業再打電動）、밥을 먹고 나서 이를 닦아요（吃完飯刷牙）。
explain.en: The first action is fully finished before the next one starts: 숙제를 하고 나서 게임을 해요 (I play games after finishing my homework), 밥을 먹고 나서 이를 닦아요 (I brush my teeth after eating).

notes.zh: 和「-(으)ㄴ 후에」意思很接近；「-고 나서」更強調前一件事「做完」。
notes.en: Close to -(으)ㄴ 후에; -고 나서 stresses that the first thing is done.

notes.zh: 前面不加過去式：過去的事也說「먹고 나서 …았어요」。
notes.en: No past tense before it: for the past, say 먹고 나서 …았어요.

examples.en: I play games after finishing my homework.
I brush my teeth after eating.
We had dinner after the film.

quiz.en: I play after finishing my homework.
I went to bed after showering.

quiz.zh: 下課以後一起吃午餐吧。
quiz.en: Let's have lunch together after class.
Wash your hands before you eat.

quiz.zh: 「什麼時候看電影？」「作業全做完再看吧。」
quiz.en: "When shall we watch the film?" "After we finish all our homework."
After dinner, I go for a walk.

form.zh: 母音ㅏ・ㅗ → -아도 돼요　其他 → -어도 돼요　하다 → 해도 돼요
form.en: ㅏ/ㅗ → -아도 돼요　others → -어도 돼요　하다 → 해도 돼요

explain.zh: 表示允許「可以～」：여기 앉아도 돼요?（可以坐這裡嗎？）―네, 앉아도 돼요（可以）。
explain.en: Gives or asks permission: 여기 앉아도 돼요? (may I sit here?) — 네, 앉아도 돼요 (yes, you may).

notes.zh: 回答「可以」常簡單說「네, 그럼요」；不可以用「-(으)면 안 돼요」（下一個文法）。
notes.en: A short yes is 네, 그럼요; no is -(으)면 안 돼요 (next point).

examples.en: May I sit here?
May I take a photo?
You don't have to come tomorrow.

quiz.en: May I sit here?
May I take a photo?
You don't have to come tomorrow.

quiz.zh: 「這件衣服可以試穿嗎？」「可以，請在那邊試穿。」
quiz.en: "May I try this on?" "Yes, try it on over there."
You don't have to take your shoes off here.
May I park here?

title.zh: 試著～、～看看（嘗試；過去式是「做過」）

form.zh: 母音ㅏ・ㅗ → -아 보다　其他 → -어 보다　하다 → 해 보다
form.en: ㅏ/ㅗ → -아 보다　others → -어 보다　하다 → 해 보다

explain.zh: 試著做某件事：이 김치 한번 먹어 보세요（請吃吃看這個泡菜）。「-아/어 보세요」是建議對方試試；過去式「-아/어 봤어요」表示經驗「做過」：제주도에 가 봤어요?（你去過濟州島嗎？）。
explain.en: Try doing something: 이 김치 한번 먹어 보세요 (try this kimchi). -아/어 보세요 suggests the listener try; the past -아/어 봤어요 tells an experience: 제주도에 가 봤어요? (have you been to Jeju?).

notes.zh: 「한번」（一次、試一下）常和它一起用。
notes.en: 한번 ("once, just") often goes with it.

notes.zh: 「-아/어 본 적이 있다」也很常見：가 본 적이 있어요（曾經去過）。
notes.en: -아/어 본 적이 있다 is common too: 가 본 적이 있어요 (I have been there).

mistakes.en: 먹다 has ㅓ, so it takes -어 보다.

examples.en: Try this kimchi.
I've tried on a hanbok.
Have you been to Jeju Island?

quiz.en: Try this on.
Have you tried Korean food?

quiz.zh: 不懂的話請問問看老師。
quiz.en: If you don't know, try asking the teacher.

quiz.zh: 這雙鞋請試穿看看，真的很舒服。
quiz.en: Try these shoes on. They're really comfortable.

quiz.zh: 「去過濟州島嗎？」「還沒有機會去。」
quiz.en: "Have you been to Jeju?" "No, not yet."

quiz.zh: 去韓國的話請吃吃看辣炒年糕。
quiz.en: When you go to Korea, try tteokbokki.

form.zh: 語幹 ＋ (으)면 안 돼요
form.en: stem + (으)면 안 돼요

explain.zh: 表示禁止「不可以～」：여기서 담배를 피우면 안 돼요（這裡不可以抽菸）、수업 시간에 휴대폰을 쓰면 안 돼요（上課時不可以用手機）。
explain.en: Forbids something: 여기서 담배를 피우면 안 돼요 (you mustn't smoke here), 수업 시간에 휴대폰을 쓰면 안 돼요 (no phones in class).

notes.zh: 回答「-아도 돼요?」的「不行」就用它：아니요, 찍으면 안 돼요。
notes.en: It answers -아도 돼요? with “no”: 아니요, 찍으면 안 돼요.

examples.en: You mustn't smoke here.

examples.text: 수업 시간에 휴대폰을 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: No phones during class.
You can't take photos in the museum.

quiz.en: You mustn't smoke here.
You can't take photos.
You can't use your phone.

quiz.zh: 美術館裡面不可以拍照。
quiz.en: You mustn't take photos inside the gallery.

quiz.zh: 上課時不可以跟朋友聊天。
quiz.en: You mustn't chat with friends in class.
You must not smoke here.

form.zh: 動詞詞幹 ＋ -지 마세요（有沒有收音都一樣）　朋友間：-지 마　一起不要：-지 맙시다
form.en: verb stem + -지 마세요 (any stem)　to friends: -지 마　let's not: -지 맙시다

explain.zh: 客氣地請對方不要做某事：걱정하지 마세요（請不要擔心）、여기에서 사진을 찍지 마세요（請不要在這裡拍照）。「마세요」來自「말다（停止、不做）」。
explain.en: Politely asks someone not to do something: 걱정하지 마세요 (don't worry), 여기에서 사진을 찍지 마세요 (please don't take photos here). 마세요 comes from 말다 (to stop, not do).

notes.zh: 「안 -(으)세요」不能表示「請不要～」：안 가세요 是「您不去嗎／您不去」。
notes.en: 안 -(으)세요 can't mean "please don't": 안 가세요 means "you aren't going".

notes.zh: 「말다」遇到「-세요」變成「마세요」，不是「말으세요」。
notes.en: 말다 + -세요 is 마세요, not 말으세요.

mistakes.en: To ask someone not to, use -지 마세요.

examples.en: Don't worry.
Please don't take photos here.
Please don't be late tomorrow.

quiz.en: Don't worry.

quiz.zh: 請不要把垃圾丟在這裡。
quiz.en: Please don't throw rubbish here.

quiz.zh: 上課時間請不要看手機。
quiz.en: Please don't look at your phone in class.

quiz.zh: 「對不起，我遲到了。」「沒關係，別太在意。」
quiz.en: "Sorry I'm late." "That's all right. Don't worry about it."

quiz.q: 밤에는 커피를 마시（　）. 잠을 못 자요.
quiz.zh: 晚上請不要喝咖啡，會睡不著。
quiz.en: Don't drink coffee at night. You won't sleep.

quiz.zh: 很危險，請不要在這裡游泳。
quiz.en: It's dangerous, so don't swim here.

form.zh: 動詞・있다/없다 ＋ 는데　／　形容詞：無收尾音 ＋ ㄴ데、有收尾音 ＋ 은데　／　名詞 ＋ 인데　／　過去：-았/었는데
form.en: verb, 있다/없다 + 는데　/　adjective: no 받침 + ㄴ데, 받침 + 은데　/　noun + 인데　/　past: -았/었는데

explain.zh: 先交代背景，再說出主要的事（請求、建議、問題）：비가 오는데 우산 있어요?（在下雨，你有傘嗎？）。也可以表示對比：형은 키가 큰데 저는 작아요（哥哥很高，我卻很矮）。
explain.en: Sets the scene before the main point (a request, suggestion or question): 비가 오는데 우산 있어요? (it's raining — do you have an umbrella?). Also a contrast: 형은 키가 큰데 저는 작아요 (my brother is tall, but I'm short).

notes.zh: 放在句尾「-는데요」是委婉地留下話尾，等對方回應。
notes.en: At the end, -는데요 trails off softly, waiting for a reply.

mistakes.en: A verb in the present takes -는데.

examples.en: It's raining — do you have an umbrella?

examples.zh: 這件衣服很漂亮，但太貴了。
examples.en: These clothes are pretty, but too expensive.

examples.text: 어제 그 식당에 갔는데 문을 닫았더라고요.
examples.zh: 昨天去了那家餐廳，結果它沒開。
examples.en: I went to that restaurant yesterday, but it was closed.

quiz.en: It's raining — got an umbrella?
Pretty, but too expensive.

quiz.zh: 天氣很好，要不要去散步？
quiz.en: The weather's nice — shall we take a walk?

quiz.q: 저는 매운 음식을 좋아하（　）동생은 못 먹어요.
quiz.zh: 我喜歡辣的食物，但弟弟不敢吃。
quiz.en: I like spicy food, but my younger brother can't eat it.

quiz.zh: 外面有點吵，要不要關窗？
quiz.en: It's a bit noisy outside. Shall I close the window?

quiz.zh: 明天要去看電影，要一起去嗎？
quiz.en: I'm going to see a film tomorrow. Want to come?

form.zh: 語幹無收尾音・ㄹ收尾 ＋ 면서　／　有收尾音 ＋ 으면서
form.en: stem without 받침 or ending in ㄹ + 면서　/　with 받침 + 으면서

explain.zh: 同一個人同時做兩件事：음악을 들으면서 공부해요（一邊聽音樂一邊念書）。
explain.en: One person doing two things at once: 음악을 들으면서 공부해요 (I study while listening to music).

notes.zh: 前後主語必須相同。
notes.en: Both parts must have the same subject.

notes.zh: 듣다 是ㄷ不規則：듣 → 들으면서。
notes.en: 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular: 들으면서.

examples.zh: 我一邊聽音樂一邊念書。
examples.en: I study while listening to music.

examples.zh: 邊開車邊講電話很危險。
examples.en: It's dangerous to talk on the phone while driving.
Let's talk over coffee.

quiz.en: I study while listening to music.
Let's talk over coffee.

quiz.zh: 邊開車邊講電話很危險。
quiz.en: Phoning while driving is dangerous.

quiz.zh: 弟弟總是一邊看電視一邊吃飯。
quiz.en: My younger brother always eats while watching TV.

quiz.zh: 一邊走路一邊看手機很危險。
quiz.en: It's dangerous to look at your phone while walking.

quiz.zh: 一邊聽音樂一邊寫作業。
quiz.en: I did my homework while listening to music.

form.zh: 語幹 ＋ 거나　／　名詞 ＋ (이)나
form.en: stem + 거나　/　noun + (이)나

explain.zh: 從兩個以上的動作、狀態中選一個：주말에는 영화를 보거나 책을 읽어요（週末看電影或看書）。
explain.en: A choice among actions or states: 주말에는 영화를 보거나 책을 읽어요 (at weekends I watch films or read).

notes.zh: 名詞之間用「(이)나」：커피나 차。
notes.en: Between nouns use (이)나: 커피나 차.

mistakes.en: It goes straight on the stem.

examples.zh: 週末我會看電影或看書。
examples.en: At weekends I watch films or read.

examples.zh: 累了或不舒服的話就早點睡。
examples.en: When I'm tired or unwell, I go to bed early.

examples.text: 모르는 게 있으면 물어보거나 사전을 찾아보세요.
examples.zh: 有不懂的就問人或查字典。
examples.en: If there's something you don't know, ask or look it up.

quiz.en: At weekends I watch films or read.
I drink coffee or tea.
When tired or ill, I sleep early.

quiz.zh: 週末通常是見朋友，或是在家休息。
quiz.en: At weekends I usually meet friends or rest at home.

quiz.zh: 想送包包或錢包當禮物。
quiz.en: I'd like to give a bag or a wallet as a present.

quiz.zh: 無聊的時候會看書或散步。
quiz.en: When I'm bored, I read or go for a walk.

form.zh: 動詞語幹 ＋ 는 동안(에)　／　名詞（時間長度）＋ 동안
form.en: verb stem + 는 동안(에)　/　noun (length of time) + 동안

explain.zh: 表示一段時間內：아기가 자는 동안에 청소했어요（寶寶睡覺的時候我打掃了）。接名詞：방학 동안 여행했어요（放假期間去旅行了）。
explain.en: A stretch of time: 아기가 자는 동안에 청소했어요 (I cleaned while the baby slept). With nouns: 방학 동안 여행했어요 (I travelled during the holidays).

notes.zh: 和「-(으)면서」不同：前後主語可以不同。
notes.en: Unlike -(으)면서, the two subjects can differ.

mistakes.en: Use -는 동안, not the past modifier.
A noun goes straight before 동안.

examples.zh: 趁寶寶睡覺時我打掃了。
examples.en: I cleaned while the baby was asleep.

examples.zh: 放假期間我去濟州島旅行了。
examples.en: I travelled around Jeju during the holidays.

examples.text: 제가 없는 동안 고양이 좀 봐 주세요.
examples.zh: 我不在的時候，請幫我照顧貓。
examples.en: Please look after my cat while I'm away.

quiz.en: I cleaned while the baby slept.

quiz.zh: 放假期間去濟州島旅行。
quiz.en: I travelled in Jeju during the holidays.
Mind my cat while I'm away.

quiz.zh: 我做菜的時候，請幫忙擺一下餐桌。
quiz.en: While I cook, please set the table.

quiz.zh: 在韓國的期間交了很多朋友。
quiz.en: While I was in Korea, I made lots of friends.

quiz.zh: 我洗澡的時候來了電話。
quiz.en: The phone rang while I was in the shower.

form.zh: 語幹無收尾音・ㄹ收尾 ＋ 려고　／　有收尾音 ＋ 으려고
form.en: stem without 받침 or ending in ㄹ + 려고　/　with 받침 + 으려고

explain.zh: ① 說明意圖、目的：한국 친구를 사귀려고 동아리에 들어갔어요（為了交韓國朋友加入社團）。② 「-(으)려고 하다」＝打算～：내일부터 운동하려고 해요（打算從明天開始運動）。
explain.en: ① An intention or aim: 한국 친구를 사귀려고 동아리에 들어갔어요 (I joined a club to make Korean friends). ② -(으)려고 하다 = plan to: 내일부터 운동하려고 해요 (I'm going to start exercising tomorrow).

notes.zh: 後面不能接命令、勸誘：×사려고 가세요（要用「-(으)러」）。
notes.en: Not followed by orders or suggestions — use -(으)러 there.

examples.zh: 為了交韓國朋友，我加入了社團。
examples.en: I joined a club to make Korean friends.

examples.zh: 我打算從明天開始每天運動。
examples.en: I'm planning to exercise every day from tomorrow.
I bought a new camera to take photos.

quiz.en: I bought a camera to take photos.
I plan to exercise from tomorrow.
Let's go and buy bread together.

quiz.zh: 為了減肥，每天都在運動。
quiz.en: I'm exercising every day to lose weight.

quiz.zh: 本來週末想見朋友，但朋友生病了。
quiz.en: I was going to meet a friend at the weekend, but they were ill.

quiz.zh: 為了在韓國公司就職而學韓文。
quiz.en: I'm learning Korean to get a job at a Korean company.

form.zh: 動詞：過去 -(으)ㄴ／現在 -는／未來 -(으)ㄹ ＋ 것 같다　／　形容詞：現在 -(으)ㄴ／未來 -(으)ㄹ ＋ 것 같다
form.en: verb: past -(으)ㄴ / present -는 / future -(으)ㄹ + 것 같다　/　adjective: present -(으)ㄴ / future -(으)ㄹ + 것 같다

explain.zh: 說出推測，或委婉地表達意見：밖에 비가 오는 것 같아요（外面好像在下雨）、이 옷이 더 예쁜 것 같아요（我覺得這件比較好看）。
explain.en: A guess, or a softened opinion: 밖에 비가 오는 것 같아요 (it seems to be raining outside), 이 옷이 더 예쁜 것 같아요 (I think this one's prettier).

notes.zh: 看到跡象的推測用「-는 것 같다」，沒有根據的預測用「-(으)ㄹ 것 같다」：비가 올 것 같아요（感覺會下雨）。
notes.en: -는 것 같다 is from what you see; -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 predicts: 비가 올 것 같아요.

mistakes.wrong: 이 옷이 더 예쁘는 것 같아요.
mistakes.right: 이 옷이 더 예쁜 것 같아요.
mistakes.zh: 形容詞現在用「-(으)ㄴ 것 같다」。

examples.en: It seems to be raining outside.

examples.text: 이 옷이 저한테 더 잘 어울리는 것 같아요.
examples.zh: 我覺得這件比較適合我。
examples.en: I think this one suits me better.

examples.text: 하늘이 흐려서 곧 눈이 올 것 같아요.
examples.zh: 天陰陰的，好像快要下雪了。
examples.en: The sky's grey — it looks like it'll snow soon.

quiz.en: It seems to be raining.
I think this one is prettier.

quiz.zh: 天陰陰的，好像快下雪了。
quiz.en: Grey sky — looks like snow soon.
I think Minsu went home a while ago.
This bag seems a bit heavy.
I think the weather will be nice tomorrow.

form.zh: 語幹 ＋ 네요（ㄹ收尾去ㄹ：멀다 → 머네요）　／　動詞 -는군요、形容詞 -군요、名詞 -(이)군요
form.en: stem + 네요 (ㄹ drops: 멀다 → 머네요)　/　verb -는군요, adjective -군요, noun -(이)군요

explain.zh: 當下發現、感到驚訝：와, 한국어를 정말 잘하시네요!（哇，你韓文說得真好！）。「-군요」多是聽了說明後的理解「原來如此」：아, 그래서 늦었군요（啊，原來是這樣才遲到的）。
explain.en: Surprise at something you've just noticed: 와, 한국어를 정말 잘하시네요! (wow, your Korean is great!). -군요 often follows an explanation, “I see”: 아, 그래서 늦었군요 (ah, so that's why you were late).

notes.zh: ㄹ收尾的語幹接「-네요」時ㄹ脫落：만들다 → 만드네요。
notes.en: A ㄹ stem drops ㄹ before -네요: 만드네요.

examples.en: Wow, your Korean is really good!

examples.zh: 你家離學校還滿遠的耶。
examples.en: Your house is quite far from school.

examples.zh: 啊，原來是這樣昨天才沒來啊。
examples.en: Ah, so that's why you didn't come yesterday.

quiz.en: Wow, your Korean is great!
Your home is quite far from school.

quiz.zh: 原來是這樣昨天才沒來。
quiz.en: So that's why you didn't come.

quiz.zh: 「這是我做的蛋糕。」「哇，真好吃耶！」
quiz.en: "This is a cake I made." "Wow, it's really good!"

quiz.zh: 「那個人是我先生。」「啊，原來是您先生啊。」
quiz.en: "That's my husband." "Oh, so that's your husband."
Your Korean is really good!

form.zh: 沒有收音・ㄹ收音 → -ㄹ게요　有收音 → -을게요
form.en: no final consonant / ㄹ → -ㄹ게요　final consonant → -을게요

explain.zh: 說話者向聽的人表示「我會做」，常用來回應對方、答應或承諾：제가 도와 드릴게요（我來幫您）、내일 다시 전화할게요（我明天再打給你）。只用在「我（們）」的句子，也不能用在問句。
explain.en: The speaker tells the listener "I will", often as a reply or a promise: 제가 도와 드릴게요 (I'll help you), 내일 다시 전화할게요 (I'll call again tomorrow). Only for "I / we", and never in a question.

notes.zh: 和「-(으)ㄹ 거예요」比：「거예요」只是說自己的計畫；「-(으)ㄹ게요」是顧到聽的人、對他承諾。
notes.en: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 just states a plan; -(으)ㄹ게요 is said with the listener in mind, as a promise.

notes.zh: 發音是［께요］，但寫成「게요」。
notes.en: Pronounced [께요] but spelled 게요.

mistakes.zh: 「-(으)ㄹ게요」不能用在問句；問對方要不要一起，用「-(으)ㄹ까요?」。
mistakes.en: -(으)ㄹ게요 is never a question; to suggest doing something together, use -(으)ㄹ까요?.

examples.en: I'll help you.
I'll call again tomorrow.
I'll eat it later.

quiz.en: I'll open the door.

quiz.zh: 對不起遲到了，明天我會早點來。
quiz.en: Sorry I'm late. I'll come early tomorrow.
I'll give this book back when I've finished it.
"Who'll do the dishes?" "I will."

quiz.zh: 今天很忙，我明天再打給你。
quiz.en: I'm busy today, so I'll call you again tomorrow.
I'll come right after class.

title.en: do you want to …? / I want to … (casual)

form.zh: 沒有收音・ㄹ收音 → -ㄹ래요　有收音 → -을래요　對長輩：-(으)실래요?
form.en: no final consonant / ㄹ → -ㄹ래요　final consonant → -을래요　to elders: -(으)실래요?

explain.zh: 問句問對方想不想做：뭐 먹을래요?（你要吃什麼？）、같이 영화 볼래요?（要一起看電影嗎？）；陳述句說自己的選擇：저는 비빔밥 먹을래요（我要吃拌飯）。比較口語、親近。
explain.en: As a question it asks what the listener wants: 뭐 먹을래요? (what will you have?), 같이 영화 볼래요? (want to see a film together?); as a statement it gives your own choice: 저는 비빔밥 먹을래요 (I'll have bibimbap). Casual and friendly.

notes.zh: 和「-(으)ㄹ까요?」比：「-(으)ㄹ까요?」是提議「我們一起～好嗎」或問「我來～好嗎」；「-(으)ㄹ래요?」是問對方本人想不想。
notes.en: -(으)ㄹ까요? suggests "shall we / shall I"; -(으)ㄹ래요? asks what the listener wants.

notes.zh: 對長輩、客人要說「-(으)실래요?」：드실래요?（您要吃／喝嗎？）
notes.en: To elders or guests say -(으)실래요?: 드실래요? (would you like some?).

mistakes.en: To say what you want, use -(으)ㄹ래요.

examples.en: What will you have?
I'll have bibimbap.
Do you want to see a film together?

quiz.en: "What will you drink?" "I'll have green tea."
Do you want to go hiking together at the weekend?
I'll have gimbap.
"What will you have?" "I'll have naengmyeon."
Would you like a cup of tea, teacher?

quiz.zh: 這週末要一起看電影嗎？
quiz.en: Do you want to see a film together this weekend?

form.zh: 詞幹 ＋ -지요（口語縮成 -죠）　過去：-았/었지요　名詞：有收音 이지요／沒有收音 지요（죠）
form.en: stem + -지요 (spoken -죠)　past: -았/었지요　noun: after a consonant 이지요 / after a vowel 지요 (죠)

explain.zh: 說話者覺得對方也知道、也同意，向他確認：오늘 날씨가 정말 좋지요?（今天天氣真好吧？）。回答時也可以表示「當然」：그럼요, 알지요（當然，我知道啊）。
explain.en: The speaker assumes the listener knows or agrees and checks: 오늘 날씨가 정말 좋지요? (lovely weather today, isn't it?). In a reply it can mean "of course": 그럼요, 알지요 (sure, I know).

notes.zh: 「-죠」是「-지요」的縮寫，口語很常用。
notes.en: -죠 is the short form of -지요, very common in speech.

notes.zh: 名詞：학생이지요（학생이죠）、의사지요（의사죠）。
notes.en: Nouns: 학생이지요 (학생이죠), 의사지요 (의사죠).

mistakes.en: A noun ending in a consonant takes 이지요.
The past of 바쁘다 is 바빴-.

examples.en: Lovely weather today, isn't it?
Korean food is spicy, isn't it?
That film was good, wasn't it?

quiz.en: Studying Korean is fun, isn't it?

quiz.zh: 那個人是民秀的弟弟吧？
quiz.en: That's Minsu's younger brother, isn't it?
You were really busy yesterday, weren't you?

quiz.zh: 「韓國的冬天很冷吧？」「對，非常冷。」
quiz.en: "Korean winters are really cold, aren't they?" "Yes, very."
"This is Mr Kim, the teacher, isn't it?" "Yes, that's right."

quiz.zh: 昨天看的電影很好看吧？
quiz.en: The film we saw yesterday was good, wasn't it?

form.zh: （多為自動詞・被動詞）語幹 ＋ 아/어 있다（하다 → 해 있다）
form.en: (mostly intransitive / passive verbs) stem + 아/어 있다 (하다 → 해 있다)

explain.zh: 動作結束後，結果的狀態持續：문이 열려 있어요（門開著）、의자에 앉아 있어요（坐在椅子上）。TOPIK I 的「-고 있다」是動作正在進行。
explain.en: The result of an action continues: 문이 열려 있어요 (the door is open), 의자에 앉아 있어요 (sitting on a chair). TOPIK I's -고 있다 is an action in progress.

notes.zh: 比較：옷을 입고 있어요（穿著衣服；也可指正在穿）。穿戴類動詞用「-고 있다」。
notes.en: Wearing verbs use -고 있다: 옷을 입고 있어요.

mistakes.zh: 門開著的狀態用被動詞「열리다」＋「-아/어 있다」。
mistakes.en: The state uses the passive 열리다 + -아/어 있다.

mistakes.zh: 穿戴類動詞用「-고 있다」表示穿著的狀態。

examples.en: The window is open.
There's a photo hanging on the wall.
Grandma is sitting on the sofa.

quiz.en: The window is open.
A photo hangs on the wall.
Minsu is wearing a blue shirt.

quiz.zh: 坐在椅子上的人是我弟弟。
quiz.en: The person sitting on the chair is my younger brother.
The shop door is still closed.
There are flowers on the desk.

title.zh: 變得～、結果～了（非自己決定）

form.zh: 動詞語幹 ＋ 게 되다
form.en: verb stem + 게 되다

explain.zh: 因為外在情況而產生的變化或結果：회사 때문에 부산에 살게 됐어요（因為公司的關係，變成住在釜山）、한국 음식을 좋아하게 됐어요（變得喜歡韓國菜了）。
explain.en: A change or outcome brought about by circumstances: 회사 때문에 부산에 살게 됐어요 (I ended up living in Busan because of work), 한국 음식을 좋아하게 됐어요 (I've come to like Korean food).

notes.zh: 形容詞的變化用「-아/어지다」（下一個文法）。
notes.en: Adjectives change with -아/어지다 (next point).

mistakes.en: The past of 되다 is 됐어요 (되었어요).

examples.text: 회사 일 때문에 부산에서 살게 됐어요.
examples.zh: 因為工作的關係，我變成住在釜山。
examples.en: I ended up living in Busan because of work.

examples.zh: 看著連續劇，我變得喜歡韓文了。
examples.en: Watching dramas, I came to love Korean.

examples.text: 다음 달부터 새 회사에서 일하게 되었습니다.
examples.zh: 從下個月起，我將在新公司工作。
examples.en: From next month I'll be working at a new company.

quiz.zh: 因為工作變成住在釜山。
quiz.en: I ended up living in Busan for work.
I've come to like Korean.
It's got cold.

quiz.q: 처음에는 김치를 못 먹었는데 지금은 잘（　）됐어요.
quiz.zh: 一開始不敢吃泡菜，現在變得很能吃了。
quiz.en: At first I couldn't eat kimchi, but now I eat it easily.

quiz.zh: 因為公司的事，下個月起要在首爾工作了。
quiz.en: Because of my job, I'll be working in Seoul from next month.

quiz.zh: 看了韓劇之後喜歡上了韓文。
quiz.en: Watching Korean dramas, I came to like Korean.

form.zh: 形容詞語幹 ＋ 아/어지다（하다 → 해지다）
form.en: adjective stem + 아/어지다 (하다 → 해지다)

explain.zh: 狀態逐漸變化：날씨가 따뜻해졌어요（天氣變暖了）、한국어가 점점 쉬워져요（韓文越來越簡單）。
explain.en: A state gradually changes: 날씨가 따뜻해졌어요 (it's got warmer), 한국어가 점점 쉬워져요 (Korean is getting easier).

notes.zh: ㅂ不規則：춥다 → 추워지다、쉽다 → 쉬워지다。
notes.en: ㅂ-irregular: 춥다 → 추워지다, 쉽다 → 쉬워지다.

notes.zh: 常和「점점（漸漸）」一起用。
notes.en: Often with 점점 (gradually).

examples.en: Spring's here and it's got warmer.

examples.zh: 學韓文變得越來越有趣。
examples.en: Studying Korean is getting more and more fun.
It's got really cold lately.

quiz.en: Spring's come and it's warmer.
It's got much colder lately.
Korean is getting more fun.

quiz.zh: 開始運動後，身體變得健康多了。
quiz.en: Since I started exercising, I have become much healthier.

quiz.zh: 太陽下山了，外面漸漸變暗。
quiz.en: The sun's going down, so it's getting darker outside.
The weather is gradually getting warmer.

form.zh: 語幹無收尾音・ㄹ收尾 ＋ ㄴ 적이 있다　／　有收尾音 ＋ 은 적이 있다（常用 -아/어 본 적이 있다）
form.en: stem without 받침 or ending in ㄹ + ㄴ 적이 있다　/　with 받침 + 은 적이 있다 (often -아/어 본 적이 있다)

explain.zh: 說過去的經驗：한국에 가 본 적이 있어요（去過韓國）、김치를 만든 적이 없어요（沒做過泡菜）。
explain.en: Past experience: 한국에 가 본 적이 있어요 (I've been to Korea), 김치를 만든 적이 없어요 (I've never made kimchi).

notes.zh: 加上「-아/어 보다」更自然：먹어 본 적이 있어요。
notes.en: With -아/어 보다 it's more natural: 먹어 본 적이 있어요.

notes.zh: ㄹ收尾：만들다 → 만든 적。
notes.en: ㄹ stems: 만들다 → 만든 적.

examples.en: Have you ever been to Korea?

examples.text: 저는 김치를 직접 만든 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I've never made kimchi myself.

examples.text: 어릴 때 길을 잃은 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once got lost as a child.

quiz.en: Have you been to Korea?
I've never made kimchi myself.
I once got lost as a kid.
I've never once been on a plane.

quiz.zh: 曾經跟韓國朋友學過韓國歌。
quiz.en: I've learned Korean songs from a Korean friend.
I've seen Korean films.

form.zh: 動詞語幹 ＋ 기로 하다（多用過去 -기로 했다）
form.en: verb stem + 기로 하다 (usually past -기로 했다)

explain.zh: 自己下定決心，或和別人約好：내년에 한국에 유학 가기로 했어요（決定明年去韓國留學）、친구와 주말에 만나기로 했어요（和朋友約好週末見面）。
explain.en: A decision, or an arrangement with someone: 내년에 한국에 유학 가기로 했어요 (I've decided to study in Korea next year), 친구와 주말에 만나기로 했어요 (I've arranged to meet a friend at the weekend).

notes.zh: 「-기로 결심하다／약속하다」語意更明確。
notes.en: -기로 결심하다 / 약속하다 make it explicit.

examples.zh: 我決定明年去韓國留學。
examples.en: I've decided to study in Korea next year.

examples.zh: 我和朋友約好星期六見面。
examples.en: I've arranged to meet my friend on Saturday.
I've decided to give up drinking for my health.

quiz.en: I've decided to study in Korea next year.

quiz.zh: 和朋友約好星期六見面。
quiz.en: I'm meeting my friend on Saturday.
I've decided to quit drinking for my health.

quiz.q: 우리는 다음 주 금요일에 같이 저녁을（　）했어요.
quiz.zh: 我們約好下週五一起吃晚餐。
quiz.en: We've agreed to have dinner together next Friday.

quiz.zh: 這次放假決定不回故鄉。
quiz.en: I've decided not to go home these holidays.

quiz.zh: 決定從明天開始每天運動。
quiz.en: I've decided to exercise every day from tomorrow.

title.en: know how to … / not know how to …

form.zh: 語幹無收尾音・ㄹ收尾 ＋ ㄹ 줄 알다/모르다　／　有收尾音 ＋ 을 줄 알다/모르다
form.en: stem without 받침 or ending in ㄹ + ㄹ 줄 알다/모르다　/　with 받침 + 을 줄 알다/모르다

explain.zh: 表示是否具備某種學來的技能或方法：수영할 줄 알아요?（你會游泳嗎？）、김치찌개를 끓일 줄 몰라요（不會煮泡菜鍋）。
explain.en: Whether one has learned a skill or method: 수영할 줄 알아요? (can you swim?), 김치찌개를 끓일 줄 몰라요 (I don't know how to make kimchi stew).

notes.zh: 「-(으)ㄹ 수 있다」範圍更廣（能力、可能性）；「-(으)ㄹ 줄 알다」只講會不會方法。
notes.en: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 is broader; -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다 is about know-how.

mistakes.en: The negative is 모르다, not 없다.

examples.en: Can you swim?
I don't know how to drive.

examples.text: 한글을 읽을 줄 알지만 쓸 줄은 몰라요.
examples.zh: 我會讀韓文字，但不會寫。
examples.en: I can read Hangul, but I can't write it.

quiz.en: Can you swim?
I can't play the guitar.
I can read Hangul.
I know how to make kimchi stew.
"Can you drive?" "No, I can't."
My younger brother can play the piano.

form.zh: 形容詞語幹 ＋ 게（예쁘다 → 예쁘게、맛있다 → 맛있게）
form.en: adjective stem + 게 (예쁘다 → 예쁘게, 맛있다 → 맛있게)

explain.zh: 把形容詞變成修飾動作的副詞：맛있게 드세요（請慢用，好好享用）、글씨를 크게 써 주세요（字請寫大一點）。
explain.en: Turns an adjective into an adverb: 맛있게 드세요 (enjoy your meal), 글씨를 크게 써 주세요 (please write in big letters).

notes.zh: 「-게 하다」是使動（讓～）：아이를 웃게 했어요（逗孩子笑）。
notes.en: -게 하다 is causative: 아이를 웃게 했어요 (made the child laugh).

mistakes.en: Not the modifier 큰 — use 크게.

examples.en: Enjoy your meal.

examples.text: 뒤에서 안 보이니까 글씨를 크게 써 주세요.
examples.zh: 後面看不到，字請寫大一點。
examples.en: We can't see at the back — please write bigger.

examples.zh: 把房間打掃得乾乾淨淨。
examples.en: I cleaned the room thoroughly.

quiz.en: Enjoy your meal.
Please write bigger.
I cleaned the room thoroughly.

quiz.zh: 昨天工作到很晚，所以早上很晚才起床。
quiz.en: I worked late yesterday, so I got up late this morning.

quiz.zh: 孩子們在公園玩得很開心。
quiz.en: The children are playing happily in the park.

quiz.zh: 請把名字大大地寫在這裡。
quiz.en: Please write your name here in large letters.

form.zh: 語幹無收尾音・ㄹ收尾 ＋ ㄴ 지　／　有收尾音 ＋ 은 지 ＋ 時間 ＋ 되다/지나다
form.en: stem without 받침 or ending in ㄹ + ㄴ 지　/　with 받침 + 은 지 + time + 되다 / 지나다

explain.zh: 從某個動作發生到現在經過的時間：한국에 온 지 1년이 됐어요（來韓國已經一年了）。
explain.en: Time passed since something happened: 한국에 온 지 1년이 됐어요 (it's been a year since I came to Korea).

notes.zh: 「지」前後要空格：온 지。
notes.en: Spaced: 온 지.

notes.zh: 注意和「-는지（是否）」不同。
notes.en: Different from -는지 (whether).

mistakes.en: It takes the past modifier -(으)ㄴ 지.

mistakes.wrong: 밥을 먹은 지 두 시간이 했어요.
mistakes.right: 밥을 먹은 지 두 시간이 됐어요.
mistakes.en: Elapsed time takes 되다 or 지나다.

examples.en: It's been a year since I came to Korea.
How long have you been learning Korean?

examples.text: 그 친구를 못 만난 지 오래됐어요.
examples.zh: 已經很久沒見到那個朋友了。
examples.en: It's been ages since I saw that friend.

quiz.en: It's been a year since I came to Korea.
How long have you learned Korean?
It's been two hours since I ate.

quiz.zh: 在這家公司工作已經三年了。
quiz.en: I've been working at this company for three years.

quiz.zh: 開始學韓文已經半年了。
quiz.en: It's already been six months since I started learning Korean.

quiz.zh: 搬到首爾已經一個月了。
quiz.en: It's been a month since I moved to Seoul.

form.zh: 語幹 ＋ 기 때문에（過去 -았/었기 때문에）　／　名詞 ＋ 때문에（句子的話：-(이)기 때문에）
form.en: stem + 기 때문에 (past -았/었기 때문에)　/　noun + 때문에 (as a predicate: -(이)기 때문에)

explain.zh: 明確說出原因，語氣比「-아/어서」更強、更正式：길이 막히기 때문에 지하철을 타요（因為塞車，所以搭地鐵）。「名詞＋때문에」＝因為某事物：감기 때문에 결석했어요（因為感冒缺席了）。
explain.en: States a clear cause, stronger and more formal than -아/어서: 길이 막히기 때문에 지하철을 타요 (the roads are jammed, so I take the subway). Noun + 때문에 = because of: 감기 때문에 결석했어요 (I was absent because of a cold).

notes.zh: 後面不接命令、勸誘（要用「-(으)니까」）。
notes.en: Not followed by orders or suggestions — use -(으)니까.

notes.zh: 名詞當謂語時用「-(이)기 때문에」：학생이기 때문에（因為我是學生），和「학생 때문에（因為學生們）」意思不同。
notes.en: 학생이기 때문에 (because I'm a student) differs from 학생 때문에 (because of the students).

mistakes.en: A noun goes straight before 때문에.

examples.text: 길이 많이 막히기 때문에 지하철을 타는 게 좋아요.
examples.zh: 因為很塞車，搭地鐵比較好。
examples.en: The roads are badly jammed, so the subway is better.
I couldn't go to school because of a cold.

examples.text: 저는 학생이기 때문에 할인을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.zh: 因為我是學生，可以打折。
examples.en: I'm a student, so I can get a discount.

quiz.en: Jammed roads — the subway's better.
I missed school because of a cold.
It's raining — take an umbrella.

quiz.zh: 最近工作很多，所以不能去旅行。
quiz.en: I've got a lot of work these days, so I can't go on a trip.

quiz.zh: 昨天因為車禍，路上很塞。
quiz.en: Yesterday the roads were jammed because of an accident.
I couldn't go to work because of a cold.
